Does guidance apply only to part of a repository?

Code review is valuable, but it usually arrives too late. By the time it flags code that never should have been written, the rework has already begun. You pay for the original work, then for the fixes, the re-reviews, and the context switching: often three times the effort you already invested. As agents write more of the code, that hidden tax on speed and quality compounds.

Baz moves quality upstream. It learns how your team defines good: your patterns, your constraints, and the thousand decisions your experts make without ever writing them down. Then it checks every plan against them before implementation starts. Specialized agents carry that context into the code that does get written, so review becomes a quick confirmation instead of expensive damage control.
